method: Read cutoff-version primary PDF abstract, theorem statements, and conclusion before any future search for this question; physical PDF pages are one-indexed.

rows.source_locator: PDF pp. 1-3 abstract and Theorems 1.1-1.5; p. 24 section 6 Conclusions, explicit sparsifier-size lower-bound question
rows.source_basis: The 2018 source proves a polynomial metric sparsifier for Zero Extension with a size upper bound of order k^(s+1), then explicitly asks whether a lower bound exists and notes the related open issue of degree independent of s. The source does not prove a matching lower bound or a uniform-degree upper bound.
rows.candidate_question: For exact metric sparsifiers of Zero Extension with s labels and crossing-number parameter k, is an exponent growing with s necessary in worst-case sparsifier size, or can an exponent independent of s suffice?
rows.comparison_and_metric: formal worst-case sparsifier size as a function of k and s under the same exact-mimicking definition; lower bound versus uniform-in-s exponent upper bound
rows.falsification_gate: A valid k^Omega(s) worst-case lower bound under the source definition refutes an exponent uniform in s; a valid k^O(1) upper bound with exponent independent of s refutes necessity of growth. A bound for only s-Multiway Cut or a different sparsifier definition does not settle this question.

limitation: Targeted sections, not exhaustive page-by-page annotation. The author-defined exact metric sparsifier and parameter k must be matched in future results.
